prompt: Complete WirelessRouter at the bottom of a three-level Device hierarchy: chain the constructor arguments up two levels with super, extend describe() with super.describe(), and override the energy cost to add a 10 percent radio overhead on top of super's answer.
explanation: In a deep hierarchy each constructor is responsible only for the fields its own class declares and passes the rest upward, so one super(...) call per level moves the model and watts all the way to Device. The same pattern works for methods: super.describe() and super.monthlyEnergyCost(...) let the leaf class add to work already written above it instead of duplicating the formula. Because the overrides are found by the object's real type, a Device-typed variable pointing at a router still runs the router's versions.
hints: The constructor's first statement is a super(...) call passing model, watts and ports up one level; NetworkDevice keeps the ports and forwards the rest on to Device.
describe() should return super.describe() + " on " + band -- that reuses the middle class's text rather than rebuilding it.
For the cost, call super.monthlyEnergyCost(pricePerKwh) first, multiply by 1.1, and hand the result to the inherited round2 helper.
